function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "Out of decision calls with the block still on the table. Final measured state: eef (-0.017, 0.020, 0.812), gripper open 0.988, red block resting on the table near x=-0.02, y=+0.02, bowl at x about +0.18. Six close attempts (eef z 0.886, 0.855, 0.831, 0.814 and two aborted) all shut on empty air and never lifted the block, so nothing was placed in the bowl. The binding constraint was the 20-call limit (715 of 900 control steps used), not the step budget.", "hindsight": "Controller facts worth having before starting. (1) move_to interpolates at roughly 35 mm per control step per position axis, 0.31 rad/step for yaw and only about 0.0125 units/step for the gripper, and the number of steps executed is set by the largest single-dimension delta. The arm itself only tracks 2-5 mm per step, so a short Cartesian target of 6-10 cm buys only 1-3 steps and the arm never arrives. Bundle a full gripper open or close command with any move that must actually be completed, since that alone buys about 79 steps. A yaw flip buys only 10-20 steps and is a trap: it introduced 20-30 degrees of roll/pitch (visible in eef_quat) and dragged the measured eef up to 60 mm sideways in y, ruining the alignment every time I used it. (2) The reported gripper value saturates (0.015 closed, 0.98-0.99 open) and never showed an intermediate value even with the fingers at the block, so it cannot confirm a grasp; verify visually in the side view instead. (3) Table is at z=0.80, the block is a roughly 30 mm cube with its top near z=0.83, and the fingertips sit about 30 mm below the reported eef point (the descent stalled at z=0.831 when 0.822 was commanded and only reached 0.811 when the z bound 0.80 was commanded), so a real grasp needs eef z about 0.810-0.815 before closing. (4) Because z is clamped at 0.80 the pads can barely get below the block top, and the effective pad gap is much smaller than the nominal 80 mm, so the lateral centring tolerance is only a few millimetres, far tighter than the 2-2.5 mm/px fixed-camera scale and my roughly 10 px reading accuracy allow. One descent pushed the block about 35 mm in -x, which is the signature of the jaws landing on the block instead of around it. (5) Camera frames: side view horizontal is world x with left meaning larger x; the wrist view image up is +x and looks down and forward, so an object directly under the hand is hidden behind the fingers; the front view gives y but its sign is not self-evident. The bowl sits at x about 0.18, y about 0 with a small red marker dot on its inner floor. (6) Budget plan for a future attempt: of the 20 calls, the approach and grasp should take at most 4-5 (open plus long bundled descent, close, verify), leaving 5 or more for lift, transport (about 200 mm in x, which needs two or three dedicated calls at 80 steps each) and the release, because the block is only freed about 40-50 steps into the 80-step opening ramp, so the hand must already be over the bowl when the open is commanded."}
